revision_notes: Addresses plan review feedback: (1) includes full analysis options and rationale inline, (2) explicitly documents assumed defaults for all unresolved HITL decisions with per-task impact analysis, (3) splits oversized tasks TASK-2-1, TASK-3-1, and TASK-4-1 into appropriately scoped subtasks.
title: Architecture analysis: Conversational Claude coordinator for dynamic agent orchestration
summary: Introduce a coordinator agent that understands tasks, determines workflows, and drives the orchestrator dynamically. The recommended approach (Option A: Embedded Coordinator) adds a COORDINATOR agent role with elevated gateway permissions and coordinator-specific tools (spawn agents, monitor message bus, advance/skip phases, escalate to humans). A new SSE-based MCP server acts as a thin stateless bridge between external Claude Code sessions and the coordinator. The coordinator operates in hybrid phase mode — existing phases are advisory, the coordinator can skip/reorder them freely. The orchestrator gains new APIs for flexible agent spawning outside rigid phase sequences. Implementation is phased: v1 delivers the coordinator agent + orchestrator API extensions + MCP server; async triggers follow in v2.

analysis_options_and_rationale.description: Three approaches were evaluated during the refine phase. This section captures the full analysis so the plan reviewer can verify the recommended approach.

options.title: Embedded Coordinator — coordinator as a privileged agent container
options.approach: Add a COORDINATOR agent role that runs as a standard agent container with elevated permissions. The coordinator uses claude --print (headless mode), consistent with all existing agents. It interacts with the orchestrator via REST APIs to spawn agents, monitor progress, advance/skip phases, and escalate decisions. A new SSE-based MCP server bridges external Claude Code sessions to the coordinator.
pros: Reuses existing infrastructure (container spawning, gateway sessions, message bus, SSE streaming, checkpoint system)
Orchestrator remains single source of truth for pipeline state
Gateway enforcement is naturally preserved — coordinator is just another (privileged) agent
Incremental: existing SDLC pipeline runs unchanged; coordinator is opt-in
No new services needed beyond MCP sidecar
Follows EGG200 convention (LLM reasoning inside Claude Code sessions, not direct API calls from infra)
cons: Coordinator session lifetime bounded by Claude's context window (~200k tokens)
Container overhead while coordinator is running
Orchestrator API needs significant extensions for flexible agent spawning
Phase enforcement model needs to accommodate cross-phase coordinator

options.title: External Coordinator Service — standalone service with direct Anthropic API
options.approach: Build a new standalone coordinator service that manages a Claude session via direct Anthropic API calls and translates high-level task descriptions into orchestrator API calls.
pros: Can manage multiple pipelines from single service
Custom session persistence without container lifecycle constraints
cons: Violates EGG200 convention — makes direct Anthropic API calls from infrastructure code, bypassing the sandbox boundary (per docs/guides/agent-mode-design.md)
New service to build, deploy, maintain
Must duplicate or proxy orchestrator functionality
Requires own Anthropic API credential management
options.rejected_reason: Violates EGG200: LLM reasoning must happen inside Claude Code sessions, not via programmatic API calls from orchestration services. This is a fundamental architectural principle.

options.title: Host-Level Claude Code Session — coordinator runs on the host
options.approach: The coordinator runs as a Claude Code session on the host, using existing tools plus coordinator-specific skills. It interacts with the orchestrator via egg-orch CLI.
pros: Leverages Claude Code's native tool system
cons: May conflict with user's existing Claude Code session
Depends on Claude Code-specific features that may change
options.rejected_reason: Conflates coordinator with user's development environment. Option A can evolve into host-level mode later. Foundation should be container-based for security isolation.

analysis_options_and_rationale.recommendation_rationale: Natural evolution of the current architecture. The coordinator is just another agent with elevated permissions and coordinator-specific tools. This preserves the security model, reuses all existing infrastructure, and requires no new services beyond the MCP sidecar. The main risk (session lifetime) is mitigated by persisting state in the orchestrator and supporting checkpoint/resume.

unresolved_hitl_decisions.description: The refine phase registered 4 HITL decisions and 3 feedback questions, all currently unresolved. This section documents the assumed default for each, justifies it, and specifies exactly which tasks would change if a different option is selected.

decisions.question: Coordinator session persistence model: How should the coordinator handle long-running tasks that exceed a single Claude session?
decisions.justification: Builds on existing checkpoint infrastructure (egg-checkpoint). Balances reliability (state survives crashes) with efficiency (no constant re-spawning). The coordinator saves workflow state to orchestrator at key decision points; a crashed coordinator re-assesses from current state rather than replaying reasoning.

tasks_affected_if_different.nature_of_changes: TASK-1-4: coordinator_state schema would need a 'last_poll_timestamp' and 'next_action_queue' instead of checkpoint markers. TASK-3-1a: CoordinatorExecutor would implement a periodic respawn loop (spawn coordinator → coordinator takes one action → exits → respawn after interval) instead of long-running monitoring. TASK-3-1b: crash handling becomes simpler (coordinator is ephemeral anyway) but health monitoring adds polling interval configuration. TASK-5-1: coordinator instructions would be stateless (each invocation starts fresh from orchestrator state) rather than checkpoint-aware. TASK-5-2: prompt generation would always include full state reconstruction, not just on-resume.

TASK-1-4: coordinator_state becomes minimal (no checkpoint markers needed, context window is the state). TASK-3-1b: crash handling must notify human rather than auto-respawn (no state to resume from). TASK-5-1: coordinator instructions must emphasize compact output and context-window management strategies.

decisions.question: Phase model for coordinator-driven pipelines: Should the coordinator operate within the existing phase system, outside it, or in hybrid mode?
decisions.justification: Phases remain as an organizational concept and permission boundary, but the coordinator can skip/reorder freely. This preserves backward compatibility (non-coordinator pipelines use fixed phases unchanged) while giving the coordinator the flexibility the issue requires.

tasks_affected_if_different.nature_of_changes: TASK-2-1b: the phase endpoint would only support advance-to-next (not skip-to-arbitrary), removing the skip-to logic. TASK-3-1a: CoordinatorExecutor would track phase progression strictly (coordinator must advance through phases in order, can only skip forward). TASK-3-3: gateway permissions would use the existing per-phase permission model rather than a coordinator pseudo-phase — the coordinator gets the permissions of whatever phase it is currently in.

TASK-3-3: requires building a completely new permission model for coordinator-driven pipelines (not a pseudo-phase extension). Gateway phase_filter.py would need a separate code path for 'phaseless' pipelines. TASK-3-4: session_manager would need to handle sessions without a phase field. TASK-5-1: coordinator instructions would not reference phases at all.

decisions.question: Coordinator authority level: What should the coordinator be able to do without human approval?
decisions.justification: The issue describes the coordinator as managing the full lifecycle autonomously, escalating only for ambiguous requirements, architecture decisions, and PR readiness. This matches the 'full autonomy' option. The coordinator's authority is already bounded by guardrails (max agents, max retries, max time) which prevent runaway behavior.

tasks_affected_if_different.nature_of_changes: TASK-2-1b: the phase endpoint would create a mandatory HITL gate before advancing phases (coordinator requests advance → human approves → advance proceeds). TASK-3-1a: CoordinatorExecutor would implement a phase-boundary pause (coordinator spawns agents, waits for completion, then blocks until human approves phase transition). TASK-5-1: coordinator instructions would include mandatory escalation at each phase boundary.

TASK-2-1a: spawn endpoint would create HITL approval before actually spawning (coordinator requests spawn → human approves → container spawns). TASK-2-1b: all phase/escalate operations require human approval gates. TASK-3-1a: CoordinatorExecutor would implement approval queuing for every coordinator action. TASK-4-2: MCP tools would need an 'approve_action' tool for the human to approve queued coordinator decisions. TASK-5-1: coordinator instructions would describe an approval-request workflow rather than autonomous execution.

decisions.question: Scope of initial implementation: How much of the coordinator system should be built in the first iteration?
decisions.assumed_default: Core only (coordinator agent + orchestrator API extensions + MCP server, without async triggers)
decisions.justification: The issue explicitly marks async triggers as a follow-on concern. Building the coordinator + APIs + MCP server delivers the full interactive workflow (user submits task via MCP → coordinator manages lifecycle) while deferring Slack/webhook/CI triggers to v2.

tasks_affected_if_different.nature_of_changes: Would add Phase 6 with tasks for: Slack integration (webhook receiver, task submission from Slack messages), webhook trigger endpoint (HTTP endpoint for CI/external systems), GitHub issue event handler (label-triggered coordinator). Each requires its own authentication, rate limiting, and notification channel. Estimated 4-5 additional tasks.

All Phase 4 tasks (TASK-4-1a, TASK-4-1b, TASK-4-2, TASK-4-3, TASK-4-4) would be removed. The coordinator would be operated solely via egg-orch CLI commands, not MCP. TASK-5-1 (coordinator instructions) would document CLI-only usage. Claude Code integration documentation in TASK-5-5 would be deferred.

feedback_questions.question: What cost limits or guardrails should be applied to coordinator sessions?
feedback_questions.assumed_default: Max 10 agents per task, max 2 retries per role, configurable max wall-clock time (default 120 minutes). Orchestrator enforces limits; coordinator is terminated if exceeded.
feedback_questions.justification: These defaults prevent runaway spawning while allowing realistic multi-agent workflows. A complex feature might use: 1 coder + 1 tester + 1 documenter + 1 integrator + 2 retries = 8 agents, well within the 10-agent limit.
feedback_questions.tasks_affected_if_different: TASK-1-4 (guardrail_counters schema), TASK-2-1a (spawn guardrail enforcement), TASK-3-1b (global guardrail enforcement). Changes would be field values and threshold checks, not structural.

feedback_questions.question: What should happen when the coordinator session crashes mid-task with running agents?
feedback_questions.assumed_default: Running agents continue and auto-commit (existing behavior). Orchestrator detects coordinator exit, auto-respawns a new coordinator (up to max 2 respawns) that re-assesses from orchestrator state. After max respawns, notifies human.
feedback_questions.justification: Matches the checkpoint/resume persistence model. Running agents should not be interrupted — their work is valuable. The new coordinator inherits the same pipeline state and can make informed decisions about next steps.
feedback_questions.tasks_affected_if_different: TASK-3-1b (crash handling logic). If 'always notify human' is preferred, remove auto-respawn and replace with HITL escalation on coordinator exit.

feedback_questions.question: Should the coordinator be able to manage multiple related issues simultaneously?
feedback_questions.assumed_default: One-issue-at-a-time for v1. Each issue gets its own coordinator instance and pipeline.
feedback_questions.justification: Multi-issue coordination adds significant complexity (cross-issue dependency resolution, shared branch management, conflict detection). Single-issue coordinators can run in parallel across different issues without cross-contamination. Multi-issue support can be added in v2 as an orchestrator-level feature.
feedback_questions.tasks_affected_if_different: Would require new tasks: coordinator cross-pipeline awareness, shared state between coordinators, dependency graph management. Structural change to CoordinatorExecutor (TASK-3-1a/b) and coordinator instructions (TASK-5-1).

problem_statement.description: The current SDLC pipeline follows a rigid, fixed-phase sequence (REFINE → PLAN → IMPLEMENT → PR) driven by CLI commands and pre-configured dispatch logic. Every task traverses the same phases regardless of complexity. Phase transitions require explicit CLI invocation or GitHub Actions automation. The system cannot reason about task complexity, skip unnecessary phases, loop back after failures, or adapt workflows in real time. There is no conversational interface — all orchestration requires knowledge of egg-orch, egg-contract, and phase mechanics.

root_causes.title: Fixed phase sequencing with no adaptive routing
root_causes.description: PipelinePhase enum defines exactly four phases (REFINE, PLAN, IMPLEMENT, PR) traversed sequentially. Phase transitions are driven by explicit API calls (POST /pipelines/{id}/phase) with no logic to evaluate whether a phase should be skipped based on task characteristics.

root_causes.title: No intelligent task assessment or workflow selection
root_causes.description: The dispatch system (PipelineDispatcher in orchestrator/dispatch.py) delegates to egg_contracts.Orchestrator which returns fixed DispatchDecision objects. No mechanism to evaluate task complexity and select an appropriate workflow.

root_causes.title: No feedback loop or loopback capability
root_causes.description: When a tester finds an issue, the system cannot automatically re-spawn the coder. The message bus (#1027) enables communication but no agent has authority to act on messages by spawning new agents.

root_causes.title: No conversational interface for task submission
root_causes.description: Tasks enter via CLI (egg-sdlc, egg-orch pipeline create) or GitHub Actions. No natural language interface and no MCP server to bridge external Claude Code sessions with the orchestrator.

root_causes.title: No coordinator role in the agent model
root_causes.description: The AgentRole enum (17 roles across lines 64-87) has no COORDINATOR role. All roles are task-execution or review roles. No role has cross-phase authority.

current_architecture.execution_model: Wave-based sequential execution via MultiAgentExecutor or concurrent execution via ConcurrentPhaseExecutor. Both operate within a single phase — no cross-phase agent spawning.
current_architecture.communication_model: Completion-time handoff data (orchestrator/handoffs.py) for wave-based mode. In-memory message bus (orchestrator/message_store.py) for concurrent mode with typed messages. No external-facing message interface.
current_architecture.phase_model: Four fixed phases (REFINE → PLAN → IMPLEMENT → PR) with per-phase permissions enforced by gateway (gateway/phase_filter.py). Phase transitions require explicit API calls.
current_architecture.agent_model: 17 roles in AgentRole enum. File access per role in shared/egg_contracts/agent_roles.py. Gateway enforces role-based restrictions at commit time (gateway/agent_restrictions.py). Instructions from sandbox/.claude/rules/ templates.

key_components.name: PipelinePhase enum
key_components.description: Four fixed phases. No dynamic phase selection.

key_components.name: PipelineConfig
key_components.description: Pipeline configuration with multi_agent, concurrent_execution, max_parallel_agents. No coordinator_enabled flag.

key_components.name: Pipeline model
key_components.description: Pipeline state including status, current_phase, config, phases, decisions. No coordinator_state field.

key_components.name: StateStore
key_components.description: Git-backed pipeline state persistence. Methods: load_pipeline, save_pipeline, create_pipeline, update_pipeline. No coordinator-specific methods.

key_components.name: EventBus and EventType
key_components.description: 22 event types covering pipeline/phase/agent/container/message/consensus/HITL lifecycle. No coordinator event types.

key_components.name: ContainerSpawner
key_components.description: spawn_agent_container() accepts agent_role, pipeline_id, extra_env for extensibility. Already supports arbitrary roles via AgentRole.

key_components.name: PhaseFilter
key_components.description: Per-phase operation permissions. Phases: refine, plan, implement, pr. No coordinator pseudo-phase.

key_components.name: Agent restrictions
key_components.description: Per-role file access patterns. Security model: blocked patterns checked first. validate_agent_push() is gateway entry point.

key_components.name: SessionManager
key_components.description: register_session() creates session with token, binds container_id, mode, pipeline_id, agent_role, phase. Already accepts arbitrary agent_role strings.

key_components.name: OrchestratorClient
key_components.description: Signal methods (complete, progress, error, heartbeat, readiness) and message bus methods (send, poll, status). No coordinator-specific methods.

key_components.name: orch_cli.py
key_components.description: 10 subcommand groups (health, env, pipeline, signal, phase, decision, container, message, gateway). No coordinator subcommand.

key_components.name: API blueprints
key_components.description: 10 registered blueprints (checks, health, pipelines, containers, phases, signals, decisions, messages, metrics, webhooks). No coordinator blueprint.

key_components.name: ConcurrentPhaseExecutor
key_components.description: Spawns all agents simultaneously within a phase. Manages consensus, failure handling, per-agent worktrees. Foundation pattern for coordinator executor.

key_components.name: SSE streaming
key_components.description: Per-pipeline and unified multi-pipeline event streaming. Foundation for MCP server real-time updates.

recommended_approach.title: Option A: Embedded Coordinator — coordinator as a privileged agent container within the existing orchestrator
recommended_approach.description: Add a COORDINATOR agent role that runs as a standard agent container with elevated permissions and coordinator-specific tools. The coordinator uses Claude in headless mode (claude --print), consistent with all existing agents. It interacts with the orchestrator via REST APIs to spawn agents, monitor progress, advance/skip phases, and escalate decisions. A new SSE-based MCP server runs as a sidecar alongside the orchestrator, bridging external Claude Code sessions to the coordinator.
recommended_approach.justification: Natural evolution of the current architecture. Preserves the security model, reuses all existing infrastructure, follows EGG200 convention. Option B rejected for violating EGG200. Option C rejected for breaking security isolation.

components.name: COORDINATOR agent role
components.description: New agent role in AgentRole enum with AgentRoleDefinition in agent_roles.py. Write access only to .egg-state/agent-outputs/, blocked from source code and contracts. Elevated orchestrator API permissions (spawn agents across phases, skip/reorder phases, create HITL escalations).

components.name: Orchestrator API extensions for coordinator-driven spawning
components.description: New REST endpoints restricted to COORDINATOR role: spawn agent, cancel agent, query state, advance/skip phases, create escalations. Existing dispatch system unchanged for non-coordinator pipelines.

components.name: Coordinator gateway permissions
components.description: New 'coordinator' pseudo-phase in gateway granting cross-phase operation permissions. Coordinator cannot push to production branches, create PRs, or modify source code directly.

components.name: MCP server (SSE-based sidecar)
components.description: New SSE-based MCP server alongside orchestrator. Tools: submit_task, get_status, provide_input, list_tasks, cancel_task. Stateless — proxies to orchestrator REST API. SSE transport for multi-client support and async mode compatibility.

components.name: Coordinator agent instructions and prompt design
components.description: New sandbox/.claude/rules/coordinator.md defining coordinator operating model. Follows 'prefer what over how' and 'orientation not pre-fetching' principles.

components.name: Coordinator workflow state persistence
components.description: New coordinator_state field on Pipeline model. Structured state (workflow_type, agents_spawned, phase_decisions, escalations, guardrail_counters) persisted via state_store. Crashed coordinator re-assesses from current state.

components.name: Coordinator observability via message bus and SSE
components.description: New event types: COORDINATOR_DECISION, COORDINATOR_SPAWN, COORDINATOR_ESCALATION, COORDINATOR_LOOPBACK. Lightweight event emissions surfaced via SSE stream.

components.name: Pipeline mode: coordinator-driven execution
components.description: coordinator_enabled flag on PipelineConfig (default false). When enabled, orchestrator spawns coordinator instead of fixed-phase dispatch. Existing pipelines unaffected.

alternatives_considered.title: Option B: External Coordinator Service
alternatives_considered.rejected_reason: Violates EGG200: LLM reasoning must happen inside Claude Code sessions, not via programmatic API calls from orchestration services.

alternatives_considered.title: Option C: Host-Level Claude Code Session
alternatives_considered.rejected_reason: Conflates coordinator with user's development environment. Breaks security isolation. Option A can evolve into host-level mode later.

technical_decisions.title: Coordinator runs as agent container, not standalone service
technical_decisions.decision: Standard agent container with COORDINATOR role, using claude --print in headless mode.
technical_decisions.rationale: Preserves security model, reuses container infrastructure, follows EGG200.
technical_decisions.trade_offs: Container overhead, context window limits. Mitigated by checkpoint/resume.

technical_decisions.title: MCP server uses SSE transport, runs as orchestrator sidecar
technical_decisions.decision: SSE transport, stateless, shares orchestrator network.
technical_decisions.rationale: Multi-client support, persists across client disconnections, supports async mode.
technical_decisions.trade_offs: Network dependency. Alternative: stdio is simpler but requires co-located processes.

technical_decisions.title: Hybrid phase model — phases advisory for coordinator
technical_decisions.decision: Existing phases remain but are advisory when coordinator_enabled is true. Gateway uses 'coordinator' pseudo-phase.
technical_decisions.rationale: Backward compatible. Coordinator gets flexibility without breaking structural guarantees for other agents.
technical_decisions.trade_offs: Two execution models. Mitigated by keeping coordinator pseudo-phase minimal.

technical_decisions.title: Orientation-not-prefetching for coordinator-to-agent instructions
technical_decisions.decision: Coordinator passes task objectives, issue number, branch, focus area — not pre-fetched diffs or file contents.
technical_decisions.rationale: Per agent-mode design guidelines. Agents gather their own context. Pre-fetching wastes coordinator tokens.
technical_decisions.trade_offs: Agents spend tokens gathering context. Mitigated by specific task objectives.

technical_decisions.title: Coordinator state persists in orchestrator, not context window
technical_decisions.decision: Workflow decisions persisted as structured state in Pipeline model (coordinator_state field).
technical_decisions.rationale: Context window insufficient for multi-hour workflows. Git-backed state store provides reliable persistence.
technical_decisions.trade_offs: State serialization overhead. Coordinator must reconstruct context on resume.

technical_decisions.title: Opt-in coordinator mode via PipelineConfig flag
technical_decisions.decision: coordinator_enabled=true activates coordinator mode. Default is false.
technical_decisions.rationale: Zero risk of breaking existing workflows. Incremental adoption.

implementation_task_breakdown.description: Tasks split to address review feedback about oversized tasks. TASK-2-1, TASK-3-1, and TASK-4-1 are each split into two subtasks with clear scope boundaries.

tasks.acceptance: AgentRole.COORDINATOR exists. PipelineConfig serializes with/without coordinator_enabled. Pipeline stores/retrieves coordinator_state. Backward compatible. Tests pass.

tasks.acceptance: COORDINATOR_ROLE has correct restrictions. Registered in AGENT_ROLES. Tests pass.

Both endpoints restricted to COORDINATOR role.
tasks.acceptance: Spawn endpoint creates container with correct env. Spawn enforces guardrails (rejects when limits exceeded). Cancel stops container and records cancellation. Role validation rejects non-coordinator callers. Tests pass.

tasks.description: Add remaining coordinator endpoints to orchestrator/routes/coordinator.py: GET /api/v1/pipelines/{id}/coordinator/state (comprehensive state: phase, running/completed agents, pending HITL, message bus summary, guardrail counters), POST /api/v1/pipelines/{id}/coordinator/phase (advance or skip-to phase with reason), POST /api/v1/pipelines/{id}/coordinator/escalate (create HITL decision or feedback). Register the coordinator blueprint in orchestrator/api.py.
tasks.acceptance: State endpoint returns comprehensive data. Phase endpoint records decisions. Escalation creates HITL items. Blueprint registered. Tests pass.

tasks.description: Add coordinator client methods to shared/egg_orchestrator/client.py and types to shared/egg_orchestrator/types.py.

tasks.acceptance: CLI commands invoke correct client methods. JSON and human-readable output. Tests pass.

tasks.acceptance: coordinator_enabled=true routes to CoordinatorExecutor. False uses existing dispatch. No behavior change for existing pipelines. Tests pass.
